intro.text: April 13, 1970. Apollo 13 is about 330,000 km from Earth, two days into a smooth flight to the Moon.

captions: A bang, then the master alarm.
Swigert: “Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here.”
Lovell: “Houston, we've had a problem.”
Oxygen is venting into space. Odyssey, the command module, is dying.
The crew moves into Aquarius, the lunar module, and uses it as a lifeboat.
cutscene.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): exact wording of both quotes (about GET 55:55).

poll.question: Aquarius was built to keep two people alive for two days. Now it has to keep three alive for four. What do we do with the heat?

options.label: Shut everything down
options.hint: The cabin heads toward 3 °C. Power margin unchanged.

options.label: Keep one heater running
options.hint: The cabin bottoms out near 10 °C and the crew sleeps better. Power margin −30.

captions.text: A short engine burn puts them back on a path that loops around the Moon and home.
Behind the Moon, radio contact is lost.
They are now farther from Earth than any humans before them.

timeskip.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): GET of loss of signal behind the Moon and of the distance record.

captions: Aquarius swings around the far side of the Moon.
Radio contact with Houston is restored.
The burn home, called PC+2, is set for GET 079:27:40.

poll.question: We've come around the Moon. How fast do we go home?

options.label: Drop the Service Module and burn harder
options.hint: Home about 24 hours sooner, but the heat shield is left exposed to the cold.
options.note: Considered in 1970 and rejected, because the Service Module protected the heat shield from the cold of space.

captions.text: CO2 is climbing. The LM's scrubbers were sized for two people.

captions: The CO2 caution light comes on.
The command module's square filter canisters don't fit the lunar module's round sockets.
Engineers in Houston work out an adapter from parts on board: plastic bags, cardboard, a hose and tape.
cutscene.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): when the adapter procedure was read up (SPEC says about GET 90) and the parts list.

poll.question: The ground team's adapter isn't fully tested yet. Do we build now or wait?

options.label: Wait for the tested procedure
options.hint: CO2 climbs to about 15 mmHg first, then falls to a safe level.

options.label: Build our own version now
options.hint: CO2 peaks near 10 mmHg, but a leaky seal keeps it a little higher. The crew tires faster.

captions.text: Haise reports that their do-it-yourself canister change is complete.
captions.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): who made this report and at what GET.

captions: To save power, almost everything is switched off. The cabin is dark, cold and wet.
Water isn't just for drinking. The lunar module needs it to cool its electronics.

poll.question: How much water do the crew drink?

options.label: Strict ration
options.hint: About 0.18 L (6 oz) per person a day. Saves water, but the crew dehydrates.

options.label: Moderate ration
options.hint: About 0.5 L per person a day. Better for the crew, with less water left at the end.

captions.text: A manual course correction, steered by keeping Earth's day/night line steady in the window.
Aquarius starts recharging Odyssey's reentry batteries.
captions.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): SPEC says day 5; the GET when charging started.

poll.question: Odyssey is frozen and wet inside. When do we power it up?

options.label: As late as possible
options.hint: Saves power. The cabin stays cold and wet.

options.label: Early, to warm and dry the cabin
options.hint: About 5 °C warmer and drier for the final hours. Power margin −20.

captions: The crew jettisons the Service Module and sees the damage for the first time.
Lovell: “There's one whole side of that spacecraft missing!”
service_module.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): exact wording of Lovell's line (about GET 138:02).

steps.title: LM jettison
captions: Aquarius is released. “Farewell, Aquarius, and we thank you.”
steps.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): who said the farewell line (likely CAPCOM Joe Kerwin).

steps.title: Entry
captions: Odyssey enters the atmosphere.

steps.title: Blackout
captions: Radio blackout. Usually about four minutes; this one lasted about six.

steps.title: Contact
captions: Contact restored.
Three main parachutes open.

steps.title: Splashdown
captions: Splashdown in the South Pacific.

reentry.fact_check: TODO(fact-check): GET offsets for blackout start and contact (blackout about six minutes).

scorecard.title: Every path brings them home. How much margin did you leave them?

rows.label: Drinking water per person
rows.history: About 0.18 L (6 oz) a day, a fifth of normal

rows.label: Haise's infection
rows.history: Yes, a urinary tract infection with fever

rows.label: Heat shield exposed
rows.history: No, the Service Module stayed attached until near the end

scorecard.closing: The real crew made it home with almost nothing to spare.
